messages:
sarah: heads-up — saw a billing delta for org/ACME during last deploy window, looks like token counts are inflated for requests that trigger tool calls + retries. attaching a tiny log excerpt.

sarah: ```
2026-03-12T18:04:02Z INFO request_id=01F... prompt_tokens=48 completion_tokens=120 total_tokens=168 status=200
2026-03-12T18:04:04Z INFO request_id=01F... prompt_tokens=48 completion_tokens=118 total_tokens=166 retried_from=200
```

sarah: in this case the same logical request_id was retried by the router but both attempts appear in billing with completion tokens counted twice.

miguel: do we have repro steps + request_ids? I can run an ad-hoc reprocess if we can identify window. Is this only for tool-calls? :thinking_face:

sarah: repro is easy — curl to /v1/chat with a tool call that triggers a sync tool response + transient 502 from the tool. router retries once. I'll paste example: 

sarah: ```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"call_tool:weather(city=sf)"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
```

priya: quick question: where are tokens currently accounted? ingress proxy (api-gateway) emits events for billing, and runtime emits per-output events. If both emit without a dedupe key we double-count.

jake: the console aggregates billing events and groups by request_id if present. Looks like some runtime paths don't include the original request_id when the router does a retry-to-different-node.

maya: confirmed. telemetry pipeline currently dedupes on (org, timestamp, route, request_id) but request_id is sometimes missing or replaced on router retry. Also tool-call subprocesses log their own completion tokens as separate events.

priya: two potential fixes: 1) ensure the router carries a stable X-Redwood-Request-Id header across retries and make that the canonical dedupe key; 2) change billing emitter to tag tool-invocation-derived tokens as child tokens and only attribute them once per root request.

miguel: prefer (1) first — cheap and fixes retries across the board. (2) needed too for tool outputs that are asynchronous/streaming.

jake: console UX thought — we should surface a "dedupe applied" flag in the usage drilldown and break out prompt vs completion vs tool-output tokens so customers see where counts came from.

sarah: agree. also need to decide whether retries should be billed at all if they are automatic router retries (we probably should only bill final successful attempt, unless partial completion produced output charged to user).

priya: implementation plan:
- router: propagate X-Redwood-Request-Id unchanged when retrying, and attach original_attempt_index header.
- runtime/billing-emitter: treat events with same X-Redwood-Request-Id as dedup candidates; prefer event with final status=200 or highest completion_tokens if both returned.
- telemetry: add per-step token kind labels: "prompt", "completion", "tool_input", "tool_output".

miguel: action items: I'll run a reprocess for 2026-03-12 18:00-18:20 window after priya flips router change in staging. If dedupe logic is in place we can re-run billing pipeline to correct invoices.

priya: I'll open PR to set header and add tests. also will add an integration test that injects a 502 at tool call and asserts only one set of completion tokens attributed.

jake: I'll add console UI mock to the usage modal with the token-kind breakdown, link to support doc explaining tool-output semantics.

sarah: quick note on retries+burst controls: current burst limiter counts tokens at ingress instantaneously which can cause temporary throttle if a second attempt happens. After dedupe we should still count bursts by unique request ids to avoid double-throttling.

maya: agreed — telemetry update will also emit "dedupe_applied=true/false" per aggregated record so ops can verify.

miguel: thanks all — please tag me on the PRs. leaving a :thumbsup: reaction if no objections.

sarah: 👍
